author: BBC News
description:
Last week saw what could be the biggest heist in history: $6.3bn was stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance.

North Korean hackers are suspected of being behind the attack, which saw billions of dollars disappear in just 20 minutes.

It’s far from the first time North Korea has been accused of a major cyber-attack. Over the past decade, hackers linked to the country have targeted banks, public institutions and even Sony Pictures.

On The Global Story, Asma Khalid speaks with journalist Geoff White, host of the BBC investigative podcast The Lazarus Heist. He explains how this isolated country become a major player in the world of cyber-crime – and where all that money goes.

author: BBC News
description:
The tech giant Nvidia says it will conduct an investigation into reports that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. Mr Huang is a close advisor to President Donald Trump, and US intelligence agencies reportedly briefed the White House about the relationship. 

Nvidia is one of the world's most valuable companies, providing chips to leading artificial intelligence developers including OpenAI and Meta. China and the US are engaged in a race for AI supremacy, which has implications for everything from economic development to the future of warfare. 

Plus, we speak to our South Asia expert about former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who is contemplating a return home after two years of self-imposed exile in India. Hasina was overthrown by student-led protests two years ago, and now faces a death sentence in Bangladesh. Officials there have refused her request for a new passport, and said she should be extradited. 


00:00 Introduction
title: Nvidia's alleged Chinese spy affair and why Hasina may return to Bangladesh | Global News Podcast

Drug trafficking in France generates €7bn a year and rising - and narcotics are flooding into cities like Marseille, fueling violence on its streets.

After months of trying, a BBC team managed to enter this dangerous world - centred on deprived streets and high-rise housing estates in the port city, which police do not enter lightly.

We found an environment where ruthless gangs lure vulnerable young people with promises of easy money, but end up trapping them in a world of drug dealing, brutality and exploitation.

author: BBC News
description:
A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say.
 
The 24-year-old was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday, and died early on Monday morning, police said.
 
Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.
 
Officials initially reported the gunman had apparently been inspired by "far-right ideologies", but have since said they are still investigating any possible motivation.

author: BBC News
description:
The top Democrat widely expected to be the next US House of Representatives Speaker has said he is "a hard yes" for impeaching Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.
 
New York congressman Hakeem Jeffries told ABC's programme This Week that Hegseth had "abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran".
 
Outgoing Republican congressman Thomas Massie, a foe of President Donald Trump, has said he plans as early as Monday to introduce a resolution to impeach Hegseth, which could result in his removal from office.
 
The Pentagon told the BBC it had followed the law and that Hegseth would not be deterred by "phony investigations".
 
President Donald Trump defended Hegseth on Sunday and pushed back againt Democrats' calls to impeach the Pentagon chief.
 
"They want to impeach him. Very unfair," Trump told CBS News' 60 Minutes. "We had two wars, we won both. We won Venezuela, we won Iran."

Subscribe to our channel here: https://bbc.
title: Top House Democrat 'a hard yes' on impeaching Pete Hegseth | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
US tech giant Nvidia has opened an independent investigation following reports its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
 
The company, one of the most valuable in the world, says its board has no reason to believe Nvidia's secrets or national security were compromised.
 
US intelligence officials believe Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to the New York Times.
 
Huang has separately admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
 
US President Donald Trump says he has not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged.
 
"I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters late on Sunday, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".
